The energy density and angular distribution of power radiated by a quark undergoing circular motion in strongly coupled N=4 super Yang-Mills theory is computed using gauge/gravity duality.
The results are qualitatively similar to synchrotron radiation produced by an electron in circular motion in classical electrodynamics.
At large velocities, the quark emits radiation in a narrow beam along its velocity vector with a characteristic opening angle scaling as 1/γ and radial thickness scaling as 1/γ^3.
The total power radiated by the quark is given by the vacuum result P = a^2 √λ / (2π), where a is the quark's proper acceleration and λ is the 't Hooft coupling.
The radiation falls off as 1/r^2 and propagates radially outward at the speed of light, without any broadening or isotropization.
The entire pattern of energy density rotates with the constant angular frequency ω = v/R_0, where v is the quark's velocity and R_0 is the radius of the circular orbit.
Negative energy density is observed before and after the radiation pulse, which the authors attribute to quantum effects.
The authors suggest that extending this calculation to nonzero temperature could provide insights into jet quenching in the strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma of QCD.
Previous studies had found isotropization of radiation at strong coupling, but this work shows the radiation from an accelerated test charge does not exhibit this isotropization.
The authors are able to reliably calculate the real-time, strongly coupled radiation pattern using a classical gravitational calculation in the AdS spacetime dual to the N=4 super Yang-Mills theory.
